comparison: Perfect agreement on study system characterization (C1-C9). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers find the description of the two morphs and their developmental differences well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'dense and appropriately replicated sampling' with no concerns raised.

Strong agreement on RNAseq results showing transcriptome differences (C10-C13, C64-C65). Both find the quantitative results convincing. Peer reviewers note the 'surprisingly modest differences' were unexpected but accept the findings, while OpenEval considers the maternal provisioning interpretation (C13) reasonable though inferential.

Full agreement on gene expression classification and heterochrony findings (C14-C17, C22-C24, C44). Both evaluations find the categorization methodology sound and the conclusion that heteromorphy predominates over heterochrony well-supported by quantitative data. No methodological concerns raised by either.

Agreement on GO enrichment results and functional interpretation (C18-C19, C69-C73). Both find the enrichment patterns consistent with known biological differences. OpenEval specifically validates the cluster switching analysis, while peer reviewers accept findings without challenge. Note: peer R4 includes C37 not in OpenEval R4.

Disagreement on morph-specific gene analysis (C20-C21, C74-C78). OpenEval finds claims supported with reasonable interpretation, while peer Reviewer 2 raises significant concerns about potential methodological bias from mapping LL reads to PP genome and data-cleaning criteria that may have missed true LL-specific genes.

Agreement on F1 expression patterns (C26-C28, C79, C81-C83). Both find the results supported, with peer reviewers identifying F1 analysis as 'a major strength.' Both note the unexpected paternal bias in early stages. OpenEval includes C84 on statistical power not mentioned in peer review.

Both express uncertainty about regulatory architecture conclusions (C30-C32, C43, C45). OpenEval explicitly flags concerns about small sample size (143 genes) and unvalidated representativeness assumptions. Peer reviewers indirectly question robustness through concerns about F1 analysis methodology and request more thorough statistical reporting.

Related to F1 analysis methodology (C86-C89). OpenEval flags concerns about small sample size affecting regulatory mode assignments. Peer Reviewer 2 directly challenges the mapping rate analysis (C52, C86-C89), questioning statistical tests and noting high variation in LL mapping rates, finding claims unsupported due to methodological issues.

Divergent evaluations of parental effects analysis (C33-C34). OpenEval finds claims supported and consistent with known biology of maternal transcript degradation. Peer Reviewer 2 expresses uncertainty due to concerns about F1 developmental timing, questioning whether offspring were collected at appropriate stages given intermediate developmental rates.

Partial overlap on parental effects and F1 timing (C94-C95). OpenEval notes the limitation to three stages for LP crosses as appropriately acknowledged. Peer reviewers request clarification about F1 developmental timing and phenotypes, noting missing information about full embryogenesis time course and questioning collection timing.

Both address comparison to previous egg data (C91-C92). OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting the comparison is speculative and relies on indirect evidence across studies. Peer reviewers accept the evolutionary interpretation without challenge, finding the theoretical framework appropriately cited.

Agreement on phylotypic stage interpretation (C38-C39). Both find the biological interpretation well-supported by established developmental biology principles and appropriate citations. OpenEval includes additional claims (C35-C37, C96-C99) about broader developmental biology context not separately evaluated by peer reviewers.

Agreement on evolutionary context and theoretical framework (C40-C42, C100-C104). Both find the evolutionary interpretations, reasoning about morph-specific genes, and novelty claims appropriately supported by citations and logical given the data. No challenges raised by either evaluation.

Divergent evaluations of methodological reporting (C46-C56). OpenEval finds methods clearly stated and well-documented, specifically validating mapping rate analysis (C52). Peer Reviewer 2 finds reporting insufficient, requesting more thorough statistics for RNA-seq processing and questioning appropriateness of statistical tests, rating as uncertain due to missing critical details.

Agreement on literature context (C80, C85, C90). OpenEval finds citations appropriately support general knowledge claims about misexpression and regulatory differences. Peer reviewers accept the theoretical framework without challenge. Minimal overlap (only C90) but consistent acceptance of cited literature.

OpenEval evaluates additional heterochrony-related claims (C66-C68) not separately addressed in peer review results. These are found supported as part of the core quantitative classification analysis.

OpenEval evaluates cluster switching claims (C70-C72) including Pearson correlation analysis not separately addressed in peer review. Found supported as providing quantitative validation that most expression shifts are minor.
OpenEval evaluates claim C77 about morph-specific gene patterns not separately addressed in peer review, finding it supported by Figure 6 data.
OpenEval evaluates claim C84 about statistical power impacts from paternal bias not separately mentioned in peer review, finding it a reasonable interpretation of the anomalous early paternal bias.

OpenEval evaluates broader developmental biology interpretations (C35-C37, C96-C99) about expression trajectories and phylotypic stages. Found supported though C99 is noted as speculative about unexamined later stages. Peer review addresses only C38-C39 subset.
OpenEval evaluates literature context claims C80 and C85 about misexpression and maternal vs zygotic effects not separately addressed in peer review. Found supported by appropriate citations.

Peer reviewers evaluate F1 developmental timing and phenotype reporting (C25, C6, C94-C95) with uncertainty, requesting clarification and noting missing morphological comparisons in Figure 1. OpenEval addresses C94-C95 in R8 but not C25 or the specific concern about F1 phenotypes in Figure 1.
